archetypes.name: parity-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan documents per-linter parity contracts (exit codes, regex, parser shapes) that must match six bash sources; gaps between the written contracts and actual bash behavior are the highest-probability failure mode named in the plan's own Failure modes section.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-check each per-linter parity contract in the plan against the corresponding bash source files in scope. For each linter, verify that the documented exit table, regex patterns, CLI-flag semantics, and edge-case behaviors (e.g. mermaid fail-closed vs. non-CI fallback, skill-invocations exit-2-over-1 precedence, skill-md missing-root exit-0) actually match what the bash script does. Flag any behavior present in the bash source that the plan's parity contract omits or mis-specifies. Also check whether the stdlib frontmatter-parser spec for lint-skill-invocations covers the full set of YAML shapes the pyyaml-based original accepted, and whether the mermaid resolver order (repo-local → PATH → exit 2) and `--parseOnly` probe logic match the shell implementation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: scope-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The plan defers orchestration scripts (relevant-checks.sh, check-contains-pins.sh, lint-fix-loop.sh, ship-pr.sh) and readability data files to E1 #3690 with explicit no-touch constraints; plan steps that silently widen scope or couple to deferred surfaces are a named risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every plan step for accidental scope creep into the deferred E1 surfaces: relevant-checks.sh, run-relevant-checks-captured.sh, lint-fix-loop.sh, surface-lint-fix-stderr-tail.sh, check-contains-pins.sh, scripts/ship-pr.sh, and the readability .tsv/.tsv.md data files. Verify that the Makefile compat-target design for test-lint-readability-preamble does not require modifying relevant-checks.sh or any deferred orchestration script. Check whether the test-mermaid-fragments.sh Strategy B migration (removing two cases to pytest) can be completed without touching deferred mermaid orchestration paths. Confirm that migrated-scripts.tsv append entries correctly exclude the deferred readability data files and do not manifest any deferred orchestration script. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: consumer-sweep
archetypes.rationale: Repointing six linters across pre-commit, Makefile, CI, docs, agent-lint.toml, and scattered .md prose is the widest blast-radius surface; a live reference the plan omits becomes a broken invocation after the bash sources are deleted.
archetypes.prompt_body: Enumerate every live reference to the six retired linter paths (lint-mermaid-fences.sh, lint-skill-md-flag-signature.sh, lint-readability-preamble.sh, lint-gh-body-inline.sh, lint-codex-exec-auth.sh, lint-skill-invocations.py) across all tracked files beyond what the plan explicitly names — including AGENTS.md, README.md, skills/**/SKILL.md, scripts/*.md contract siblings, and any CI workflow step not already addressed. For each live reference, check whether the plan assigns it to a specific update step; flag references the plan omits. Also verify that the lint-mermaid CI job's setup-python addition is positioned before the run step, and that the pre-commit hook for lint-skill-invocations correctly drops additional_dependencies when switching language to system. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
